summary: All five round 2 findings are closed or reduced to a nit. The three lost gate helpers exist again, and the self-test now fails when a listed helper is missing. The band plaque fits its font from var(--title-chars). The focus ring carries an important box shadow and a white outline. Gate-r5 at HEAD shows rows 15 to 19 PASS, including 32 banner cases, 7 of 7 pages, and 4 of 4 focus targets. The 9 song-row failures are not caused by Phase 2b. I found no blocker and no new defect; two nits remain. I could not re-run vitest because the shell denied the heavy-run call; the test counts rest on the Green log and the r5 gate log.
nonblocking_findings: F14 [Nit] review-a: A2-F4 (reduced) brandForbiddenVerdict (look-phase2-browser-gate.sh:405-411) now reads the status (200 or 403), but a blank page with status 200, zero chrome pairs, and zero buttons still passes (A4 type). Rationale: the r5 log shows 'brand pages 403 page th status=200 ... chrome_brand_pairs=0 ... buttons=0', so the row cannot tell the forbidden view from an empty document. The orchestrator decision that the 403 link is not chrome stands. The 404 view now needs one brand pair (brandNotFoundVerdict, with a self-test mutant) and passes with chrome_brand_pairs=1. Proposal: DEFER to Phase 3; add one visible-text or heading check to the forbidden verdict.

F15 [Nit] review-a: The ROW_HELPERS list (look-phase2-browser-gate.sh, ROW_HELPERS and missingHelpers) is a fixed list of 25 names. A helper that a row calls but the list omits (for example parseCssColor, contrastOf, guarded) is not caught by the self-test. Rationale: the defect class of A2-F1 is closed for the 25 listed names, and a lost helper still fails closed in the row (the row prints 'the row raises an error'), so this is not a vacuous pass. The C-F1b unit case scores :is() selectors with a regex that over-counts, but with an important shadow it compares only rules that also set an important shadow, and row 19 reads the computed ring in a browser. Proposal: DEFER; derive the list from the row bodies or add a ReferenceError probe.
